answer: Require each agent to post a refundable bond that is slashed if independent audits find it copying another identity’s behavior or coordinating to claim multiple rewards. A mirror check can compare response timing and task choices across accounts, while a terrace of unrelated reviewers randomly verifies a sample against the same task. Creating many accounts then means locking up capital for each one and risking forfeiture, so the attacker pays in funds and audit exposure; the willow-soft option of simply inventing names earns nothing without a bond.
